title: Lenny Hayton and handling Lena Horne's act
summary: Jones replaced Lenny Hayton as Lena Horne's conductor and learned discipline tricks from him at the Waldorf.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: That's right. I'll tell you, the only other man that I learned -- well, several people I've learned a lot from -- was Lenny Hayton, Lena Horne's husband.
In what way was Lenny helpful?
Well, when I was working for Lena I replaced him. He came out here to Hollywood to do a movie,
you know, because he had been such a big man out --

Yes. You know? So then Lena had a very tough act, you know, a tough act. I mean a hard thing. And Lenny -- I would meet Lenny, this was at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York, and I would meet Lenny early, before dinner, and we would go in the kitchen and he would go over little tricks that he knew about handling the discipline of the musicians and the things that a guy would have to know to get through an act like Lena's, you know. And he even told me about -- you know, Lena, she could get into some moods, and Lenny even told me about how to duck her moods.
I never did find out. Because she would start smiling at me and looking pretty and there wasn't nothing to duck. I didn't want to get out of the way.
But between Lenny and Ellington I learned quite a -- I learned -- I was ahead in a lot of ways already, but mainly in recording studios, you know, and -- but these were broader scopes, you know?
